content.title: FOOD FACTS THAT SOUND LIKE A PRANK BUT AREN'T
facts: **Cashews** are never sold in their shells to consumers — the shell contains a resin so caustic it's related to poison ivy and has to be steamed off industrially before it's safe to touch.
**Nutritional yeast** is a living organism that's deliberately killed during processing, yet it's one of the few plant foods that naturally delivers a full spectrum of B vitamins.
**Watermelon rind** is fully edible and in parts of the world it's stir-fried like a vegetable — it contains more citrulline, an amino acid tied to blood flow, than the red flesh does.
**Cloves** have such strong natural antibacterial power that dentists used clove oil as a numbing antiseptic for toothaches long before modern anesthesia existed.
**Star fruit** can be dangerous for people with kidney disease — it contains a neurotoxin that healthy kidneys filter out easily but damaged kidneys cannot.
**Lychee** seeds and unripe fruit have caused real outbreaks of sudden illness in malnourished children in parts of Asia, linked to a compound that drops blood sugar sharply.
**Black pepper** increases how much curcumin (the active compound in turmeric) your body can actually absorb — by a significant margin, which is why the two are so often paired.
**Follow along** – for more surprising, verified food facts like this.
content.caption:
Let's go deeper on a few of these. Cashews are processed this way because the shell contains urushiol, the exact compound found in poison ivy — which is also why true "raw" cashews sold in stores are technically never 100% raw, they're steamed first for safety. Watermelon rind holds onto citrulline, which your body can convert into arginine, an amino acid involved in relaxing blood vessels — it's actually one reason some athletes eat it. And with black pepper, the compound piperine temporarily slows down how fast your liver breaks certain substances apart, which is exactly why it makes turmeric's curcumin stick around longer in your system. Everyone's body is different, so always listen to yours.
